talk: From Agents to Scale: Engineering AI Infrastructure on GKE
description:
As AI agents and inference workloads continued to evolve, the session explored how Kubernetes infrastructure had adapted to meet the growing demands of modern AI applications.

The talk examined how Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) enabled the development of scalable AI infrastructure through secure, isolated execution environments for agents, faster workload initialization, dynamic resource adjustments, and hardware-aware scheduling. It also highlighted how intelligent inference traffic routing helped optimize model-serving workloads.

By bringing together innovations across agent execution, compute orchestration, and networking, the session demonstrated how Kubernetes capabilities could be combined to build more flexible, efficient, and scalable infrastructure for AI workloads.

talk: Engineering the Future of Kubernetes with AI
description:
The rapid adoption of AI agents and large-scale model inference is introducing new infrastructure challenges that traditional Kubernetes architectures were not designed to address alone. Workloads now require stronger isolation, faster provisioning, flexible resource management, specialized hardware access, and more sophisticated traffic distribution.

This talk explores the capabilities of Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) that address these emerging requirements. We look at how agent workloads can run in isolated execution environments, how workload startup can be accelerated, how compute resources can be adjusted dynamically, and how hardware-aware scheduling and intelligent inference routing improve overall infrastructure efficiency.

By examining innovations across the execution, compute, and networking layers, this session demonstrates how Kubernetes can serve as a foundation for operating modern AI platforms with greater flexibility, performance, and scalability.

talk: Building AI Infrastructure at Scale with Kubernetes on Google Kubernetes Engine
description:
As AI agents and model inference systems continue to evolve, their growing complexity and fluctuating resource demands are pushing Kubernetes beyond the boundaries of traditional container orchestration.

This session examines how Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) provides a foundation for building the next generation of AI infrastructure. We explore secure, isolated environments for agent execution, optimized workload initialization, live resource resizing, accelerator-aware scheduling, and intelligent inference request distribution.

Through a unified view of the agent, compute, and networking layers, we present practical architectural approaches for creating more efficient, responsive, and adaptable Kubernetes platforms capable of supporting AI workloads at scale.

talk: Orchestrating Intelligence Behind the Scenes
description: As part of the Jetisu Digital Forum 2026 DevFest, held in Taldykorgan, Kazakhstan, the session “Orchestrating Intelligence Behind the Scenes” explored the engineering and infrastructure that powered high-scale AI and machine learning workloads on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). The talk took a closer look at how intelligent workload orchestration and autoscaling worked behind the scenes, bringing together GPUs, TPUs, networking, compute resources, and inference systems to support demanding AI applications. It shed light on the complex interplay between Kubernetes, accelerated computing, and cloud infrastructure, revealing how these components worked together to deliver scalable, efficient, and reliable AI-powered solutions.

event: 1st National AI in Surgery Congress (1. Ulusal Yapay Zeka Cerrahi Kongresi)
talk: Transforming Surgical Problems into AI Projects with Google AI Agents Workshop
description:
Transforming Surgical Problems into AI Projects with Google AI Agents Workshop.

The workshop focuses on moving beyond using artificial intelligence merely as a conversational Q&A tool, demonstrating how clinical workflow challenges and surgical research questions can be formulated into production-ready, agentic AI projects.

Session Agenda (60 Minutes):
1. Framing Surgical Problems as AI Problems: Scoping and decomposing clinical research challenges into modular, AI-addressable components.
2. Live Agentic AI Workflow: Exploring multi-agent orchestration without code—watching an orchestrator agent collaborate with specialized sub-agents handling literature/evidence discovery, clinical guideline retrieval, and evidence synthesis to contrast basic single-prompt chatbots with multi-step agentic systems.
3. Live Surgical Research Case Study: Working through an actual surgical inquiry, demonstrating problem decomposition, automated literature exploration, knowledge source querying, and evidence consolidation.
4. Hands-on Participant Implementation: Interactive blueprinting on participants' own laptops using a structured design framework (Problem → User → Input → Output → AI Tasks → Tools/Knowledge Sources → Expected Outcomes → Next Steps), leaving clinicians and researchers with actionable, concrete project concepts.
5. Multimodal AI & Computer Vision Demo: Demonstrating how foundation vision models analyze surgical video and imaging data, integrating visual modalities into surgical intelligence workflows.

event: 1st National AI in Surgery Congress (1. Ulusal Yapay Zeka Cerrahi Kongresi)
talk: The Next Era of AI in Healthcare
description:
As part of the First National Congress on Artificial Intelligence in Surgery (UYZCK 2026), the keynote session The Next Era of AI in Healthcare explored the evolving role of artificial intelligence in healthcare and its potential to transform clinical practice, medical research, and surgical workflows.

The session highlighted Google's healthcare AI initiatives and research, including Gemini, Google DeepMind's work in health, AMIE, and MedGemma. It also introduced key Google Cloud capabilities, including Vertex AI and agentic AI technologies, demonstrating how these tools can support the development of intelligent applications, clinical decision-support systems, medical research workflows, and next-generation healthcare solutions.

The session emphasized practical opportunities for healthcare professionals to use Google's AI ecosystem to explore new ideas and translate clinical challenges into technology-enabled solutions.
